title: Skinny: revert previous change
description:
Edit .in files to say "Generated automatically" so that scripts can tell
the the dissector is generated.

N.B.  I installed cog.py but could not readily successfully regenerate..

notes.body: What issue do you have with cog.py ?

I get this.  Haven't dug into it at all.


martin@martin-VirtualBox:~/wireshark$ cog.py -D xmlfile=tools/SkinnyProtocolOptimized.xml -d -c -o epan/dissectors/packet-skinny.c epan/dissectors/packet-skinny.c.in

Traceback (most recent call last):

  File "epan/dissectors/packet-skinny.c.in", line 109, in <module>

    skinny = xml2skinny.xml2obj(xmlfile)

  File "/home/martin/wireshark/tools/parse_xml2skinny_dissector.py", line 1051, in xml2obj

    return builder.root._attrs.values()[0]

TypeError: 'dict_values' object is not subscriptable

martin@martin-VirtualBox:~/wireshark$

> What distro ?

Something called "macOS"; the version of that distro is 11.6.4:

```
$ python3 --version
Python 3.8.2
$ cog.py -D xmlfile=tools/SkinnyProtocolOptimized.xml -d -c -o epan/dissectors/packet-skinny.c epan/dissectors/packet-skinny.c.in 2>&1 | tee cog.out
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "epan/dissectors/packet-skinny.c.in", line 109, in <module>
    skinny = xml2skinny.xml2obj(xmlfile)
  File "tools/parse_xml2skinny_dissector.py", line 1051, in xml2obj
    return builder.root._attrs.values()[0]
TypeError: 'dict_values' object is not subscriptable
```

Perhaps other platforms and other versions of Python may have the same issue.

https://nedbatchelder.com/code/cog/ says:

> Cog requires Python 2.7, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, or Jython 2.5.

but that's what's running on my machine, and probably what's running on Martin's machine.
My ubuntu VM is sporting Python 3.9.7

This was reported back in October 2021:

https://www.wireshark.org/lists/wireshark-dev/202110/msg00081.html

and a followup indicates that it was with Python3:

https://www.wireshark.org/lists/wireshark-dev/202110/msg00083.html

so perhaps tools/parse_xml2skinny_dissector.py needs to be Python3ified.

And, yes, cog.py is getting run by python3:

```
$ head -1 `which cog.py`
#!/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/python3
```
